synthesis.description: Volume and accounting staff circulate a tentative close schedule for the coming month, then revise and reissue it after discussion with the people involved. During the close, requests go out to clear intercompany items, resolve Sitara volume variances, set up missing deals, report outstanding expenses and confirm last-day files are complete. Treasury-style notices report amounts moved to or released from Schedule C each night, and late differences are investigated before they are written off.
steps: Circulate the tentative close schedule for the coming month.
Revise and reissue the schedule after discussion, including the cut-off after which no changes can be made.
Send lists of deals with volume variances or one-sided entries to schedulers and logistics for correction.
Ask for missing deals to be set up and intercompany balances to be cleared.
Collect outstanding expense items and confirmation that last-day files are complete.
Report nightly amounts moved to or released from Schedule C.
Investigate remaining differences and decide whether to write them off.
synthesis.approach: Publish the close calendar from one shared template with fixed cut-off times, and generate the variance and unmatched-deal list automatically from the deal and volume systems so each scheduler receives only their exceptions. A tracker of open close items (intercompany, expenses, last-day files) would show who has confirmed completion.
synthesis.rationale: The rounds repeat the same items every month: schedule, cut-off, variances, intercompany, expenses, last-day file. A close checklist with owners and cut-offs addresses the confusion over when changes are allowed and the follow-ups on unanswered items.
